slides.title: Loops save work
slides.text: Seven move blocks in a row works, but it is clumsy. A repeat block runs the blocks inside it as many times as its number says.
slides.alt: A repeat 7 times block with one move inside crosses Bolt's whole row; written out longhand it would take seven blocks.

slides.title: A loop inside a loop
slides.text: Put a repeat inside another repeat and you have a nested loop. The inner loop runs all the way through every time the outer loop goes round once.
slides.alt: A repeat 3 times bracket holds a second repeat 3 times bracket with move inside it, then turn right: a loop in a loop.

slides.title: A staircase
slides.text: The inner loop makes one stair; the outer loop makes the staircase. To count the moves, multiply: 3 stairs of 2 moves is 6 moves, not 5.
slides.alt: The nested-loop program beside a walled staircase board: the inner repeat climbs, the turn starts the next step up.

slides.title: Predict before you run
slides.text: A repeat 5 around a repeat 3 with pick up inside makes 5 × 3 = 15 pick-ups. Multiply first, then press Step to check.
slides.alt: A nested repeat program next to a staircase of gems: repeat 3 times outside, repeat 2 times with move and pick up inside.
slides.say: A repeat 5 around a repeat 3 with pick up inside makes 5 times 3, which is 15 pick-ups. Multiply first, then press Step to check.

words.means: steps that repeat a set number of times
the loop inside; it runs fully each time round
the loop outside; it decides how many times the inner one runs

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Robo Route at Loops and finish 5 levels, so you build at least one nested loop. Aim for the fewest blocks.
slides.alt: A repeat 7 times block with one move inside crosses Bolt's whole row; written out longhand it would take seven blocks.
